howDoI.q: How do I make water that moves, by turning a block into the next one round and round?
How do I make one animated block move a whole sea?
How do I make ripples roll, instead of the whole sea turning at once?
How do I make waves run up the sand and back?
How do I make round shore corners?
How do I make the waves roll along a beach?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Waves on the Shore is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. This one is about water that moves. It has two short levels. Level 1 crosses a sea on a pier. Level 2 walks round a beach. Each takes a minute or two.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each thing in the levels is made.

The keys

The Up, Down, Left and Right arrows walk. F2 shows your lives, hit points and score. Walk into the doors at the end of a level to go on.

Nothing in this game can hurt you. The water is deep, so it stops you. For water you can swim in, see Under the Surface.

pages.head: Level 1: Open Water
pages.html:
Level 1: Open Water

You start on a platform of planks. ONE BLOCK, STAMPED OVER AND OVER stands beside you. A pier of planks crosses a sea. The first stretch of the sea is one block laid everywhere, so every wave in it moves together. SAME START stands on the middle platform. The second stretch is laid from four blocks, so the ripples roll across. 4 STARTS stands on the last platform, beside the doors.

Walk off the pier and the water stops you. It is drawn as water, so nothing invisible is in your way.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • A loop of blocks. A block can turn into another block after some time, and that is the only animation Game-Maker has. Open one.bbl in the blocks editor and pick sea.0. Its Next block is sea.1 and its Time is 5 ticks (there are 18.2 ticks in a second). sea.1 turns into sea.2, sea.2 into sea.3, and sea.3 back into sea.0. Round it goes for as long as the level runs.
  • The frames. Each picture has the same two wave crests, five rows further down, so after four frames they have moved the whole 20 rows of the block and the loop closes without a jump. Blocks laid side by side join up, because each frame is the same pattern repeated every 20 pixels.
  • Why one block is a whole sea. The map holds a block number in each cell. The game keeps one clock for each block number, not for each cell, so when sea.0 turns, every sea.0 on the map turns in the same tick. The first stretch of sea is only sea.0, so it moves all together, like a sheet sliding.
  • Four starts. The loop's four blocks are also four starting points: sea.2 begins on frame 2, and goes on round the same loop. The second stretch lays them in a diagonal pattern (the remainder of its column plus its row, divided by four, decides which). Same art, same timing, and no two neighbors are on the same frame, so the water ripples.
  • Solid water. All four are solid, so the pier is the only way across. The planks are a plain block with nothing to do.
  • The signs. They are ordinary blocks with words in their pictures, set on the planks.

pages.head: Level 2: The Shoreline
pages.html:
Level 2: The Shoreline

The beach is an island of sand. THE EDGE BLOCKS ARE A LOOP stands where you start. Look along the north edge: a wave runs up the sand and back, over and over. ROUND CORNERS stands beside the cove, the bay cut into the beach. EACH EDGE STARTS AT ITS OWN FRAME stands before the point, a strip of sand that runs out into the sea. The doors are at the end of it.

Walk up to the water and it stops you. The wet sand and the foam are only pictures. You can walk through them.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • The edge is a loop. Every sand block that touches water has four blocks in two.bbl, named like shore1.0 to shore1.3. They turn into each other like the sea, but their frames last different times (8, 5, 9 and 5 ticks), so the wave rushes in, rests at the top, slides back and rests at the bottom. Frames 1 and 3 are the same picture.
  • Wet sand and foam. Each frame is drawn from one rule: the wave reaches so many pixels into the sand (4, 8, 12, 8), with a rim of white foam, and the sand beyond is darker as far as the wave goes. The edge is a little wavy, and the wave repeats every 20 pixels, so the next block joins up.
  • One loop for each shape. A block's shape depends on which of its eight neighbors are water. A straight edge, each corner, the cove and the point each need a loop of their own, so the map uses ten. The rest of the sea and the beach is plain blocks.
  • Round corners. Where two sides of a sand block are water, the sand is rounded off with a circle. Where only the corner touches water, a round bite is taken out.
  • The roll. Along the beach each stretch of three blocks starts on a different frame of the loop, so the waves arrive one stretch after another.
  • The end. Two doors at the end of the point each have a scene link to the ending in sh.gam.

pages.head: What it cannot do
pages.html:
What it cannot do

These are the engine's limits, so you can plan around them.

  • It cannot move one block and leave the next. The clock belongs to the block number, so every cell of one block changes in the same tick. Out-of-step water needs a copy of the loop for each start, as the second sea has.
  • It cannot slide a block smoothly. A block only turns into another block. A wave is as smooth as the frames you draw, and each frame costs a block of your 150.
  • It cannot make water you can swim in. These blocks are only pictures that change. Whether Kit can wade in is about the block's rules; Under the Surface shows water that pulls and floats.
  • It cannot tell when a wave is in. The game does not know what frame a block is on, so nothing can happen when the wave reaches Kit.
  • It cannot loop two clocks together exactly. Frames with different times drift against each other and meet again in time. That is fine for waves.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • Open one.bbl and redraw the four sea blocks in another color: a pond, or lava.
  • Change the Time of sea.0 to 20 and watch the water go lumpy; the other three still use 5.
  • In one.map lay sea.1 in a row and sea.3 in the next.
  • In two.bbl give the frames of one shore loop different times.
  • Draw a boat in a loop of its own and lay it on the sea.

The home page's Starters tab has more small games like this one.
